name: Salvia
grown_as: A hardy herbaceous salvia (Balkan clary). William's library holds three salvias under this name: Salvia nemorosa (entered as 'Royal Bumble Balkan Clary', 40 to 60 cm), Salvia microphylla (a shrubby salvia, 0.8 to 1.2 m, small red or pink flowers) and 'Salvia Amisiad', probably Salvia 'Amistad' (1 to 1.5 m, large deep purple flowers with near-black calyces). 'Royal Bumble' is the name of a red shrubby salvia, not a Balkan clary. Drawn as Salvia nemorosa. ⚠️ CHECK which salvia the drawing should be.
habit: An upright clump 40 to 60 cm tall and 30 to 50 cm across, of many square stems, each topped by one or a few narrow upright flower spikes, so the clump looks like a crowd of violet candles.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite pairs on square stems, each pair at right angles to the last; a tuft of larger leaves at the base
leaf.outline: Narrowly oval to lance-shaped, 4 to 10 cm long
leaf.margin: Small, rounded, even teeth (scalloped) all the way round
leaf.veins: A network pressed in from above, making the surface finely wrinkled
leaf.surface: Wrinkled, finely hairy and slightly rough; aromatic when crushed; paler beneath
leaf.stalk: Lower leaves on short stalks; upper leaves stalkless, almost clasping the stem

flower.form: A small two-lipped flower: a hooded upper lip arching over a spreading three-lobed lower lip
flower.petals: Five petals joined into a short tube, opening into the two lips
flower.centre: Two stamens hidden under the hood; the style pokes out a little
flower.behind: A purplish two-lipped calyx; at each whorl small, purple-tinted bracts that stay on after the petals drop, so the spike stays coloured
flower.carried: In whorls of a few flowers, stacked close together up dense, narrow, upright spikes 10 to 20 cm long at the stem tips
flower.season: June to August, again in September if cut back after the first flush

fruit: Four small nutlets sit in the bottom of each dry calyx, which turns brown on the spike. Seeds are round-oval, smooth, dark brown, about 1.5 to 2 mm.
seedling: Two rounded seed leaves on short stalks, then opposite pairs of small, wrinkled, toothed true leaves
winter: Dies down to a low tuft of small, grey-green, wrinkled leaves at the base, with the old stems cut back or standing brown.

leaf: narrow oval leaf with small rounded teeth all round
bloom: small two-lipped flowers: a hood over a three-lobed lip
stacked in whorls up a narrow upright spike with purplish bracts
seedling: first true leaves in an opposite pair, wrinkled and toothed
young: a leafy clump of opposite grey-green wrinkled leaves
square stems just starting to rise
flower: an upright clump of many narrow violet spikes held above the leaves
seedhead: spikes of brown dry calyces in whorls, petals gone
dormant: a low tuft of small grey-green leaves at the soil
old stems cut back or standing brown

look_alikes: Catmint (Nepeta) has softer, greyer, heart-shaped leaves and looser lavender-blue spikes with no coloured bracts. Lavender has narrow untoothed leaves on a woody bush. Meadow clary (Salvia pratensis) has much larger basal leaves and bigger flowers, 2 to 3 cm, in looser spikes. Salvia × sylvestris garden forms are almost the same.
